comparison_intro: Convert valid numeric and English date text while preserving source strings. Compare calendar dates and result types across languages.

language_notes.sas: Macro transform supplies source/result names. Standalone reference uses LOCALE=en_US; numeric dates are displayed with DATE9.
language_notes.python: english_dates uses pd.to_datetime with %d%b%Y and temporarily sets LC_TIME=C. Returned date_value stays datetime; out is a copy.
language_notes.r: Inside translate, on.exit restores LC_TIME. Numeric values use as.numeric; as.Date returns Date objects. Source text is preserved.

semantic_notes.title: A display is not a type
semantic_notes.text: 2023-01-15 can be a string or a calendar value. Test numeric and datetime/Date types as well as the displayed values.

semantic_notes.title: Added valid boundary case
semantic_notes.text: The added edge rows use -0.5, 0012, 29FEB2024 and 01MAR2024. They extend local validation, not the original prompts or trial scores.

tests.name: Original known-answer fixture
tests.catches: Wrong informat, date ordering, result values or hard-coded replacements.

tests.name: Added valid leap-day / number case
tests.catches: Integer-only conversion, loss of leap-day correctness or hard-coded fixture results.

tests.name: Preserve strings, order and types
tests.input: All CSV rows in reverse order, retaining original source strings.
tests.expected: Input unchanged; source/order preserved; numeric result and datetime/Date result.
tests.catches: In-place mutation, sorting, loss of 0012 text, or formatted strings replacing calendar values.

scope: Valid numeric strings up to eight characters and valid English DATE9 text. Calendar values are compared, not numeric storage epochs. Invalid-input policies and arbitrary informats remain outside scope.
